preArrival.simple: Use Google Flights/Skyscanner and AirAsia MOVE/Traveloka for Southeast Asian connections, then verify routes. Cambodia's official e-Visa is nationality- and checkpoint-dependent.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Phnom Penh's new Techo International Airport (KTI) is the capital gateway; Siem Reap-Angkor (SAI) serves temple-region trips. Airport and airline routes change, so confirm airport code, ground transfer, and itinerary with the carrier.

Entry: Cambodia's e-Visa, visa-on-arrival, and pre-arrival registration rules depend on nationality and entry point. Check the official eVisa portal and current immigration notices; use only official portals.

Climate and packing: Tropical wet/dry seasons bring heat, humidity, and heavy rain. Check forecasts and flood advisories; pack sun/rain protection and modest clothing for temples.

arrival24h.simple: Cambodia uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type A, C, and G outlets. Riel and US dollars are both encountered; confirm ATM fees and carry small-denomination cash.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz; Type A, C, and G sockets are reported. Check the lodging outlet and device voltage before use.

Connectivity and money: Local SIMs are available from Cambodian operators; check registration and coverage. Riel (KHR) is the currency; US dollar cash is also used in many visitor transactions. Use clean small notes and confirm current acceptance.

Airport transfer: Phnom Penh KTI and Siem Reap SAI are separate airports; confirm the airport code and current official ground transport before booking onward travel. Use official taxi/app pickup areas and agree the fare.

mobility.simple: Phnom Penh and Siem Reap rely on buses, tuk-tuks, and app-booked rides. Grab and PassApp coverage is city-specific; confirm price and destination in-app.
mobility.detailed:
City trips: Local buses serve selected Phnom Penh corridors; tuk-tuks and remorks fill many gaps. Grab and PassApp are common booking options in larger cities; verify the vehicle and displayed fare.

Intercity: Coaches connect Phnom Penh, Siem Reap, Battambang, and border towns. Check operator, station, and arrival point; road times vary substantially.

Walking and temples: Heat, traffic, and sidewalk gaps make walking tiring. At Angkor and other heritage areas, use designated paths, heed conservation notices, and plan transport between sites.

dailyLiving.simple: Nham24 and GrabFood serve parts of the larger cities; check address coverage. Use sealed water and verify pharmacy availability before rural or island trips.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Nham24 and GrabFood are options in Phnom Penh and other covered cities; enter the exact address and verify hours and payment methods. Service is limited in smaller towns.

Health and water: Use sealed bottled or properly treated water. Pharmacies vary in stock and opening hours; bring essential medication in original packaging and check import rules.

Payment and food: Cash remains useful; ABA and Wing wallets are locally important but visitor access varies. Ask about ingredients, allergens, and spice. Buffet terms are venue-specific.

socialCode.simple: At pagodas and temples, cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes where directed. Ask before photographing people or religious spaces.
socialCode.detailed:
Temples: Follow posted clothing and photography rules, remove shoes where instructed, and avoid touching sacred objects or climbing on monuments.

Home visits and dining: Ask about shoes and gifts; observe the host's lead on shared dishes. Ask about dietary needs and use serving utensils where provided.

Interactions: Khmer is the national language. A polite greeting and asking permission before photography are good defaults; customs vary by household and community.

preArrival.simple: Direct booking on Chinese carriers. Visa required (144-hour transit in some cities). Varied climate: Beijing -10°C to 30°C, Shanghai 4°C to 32°C. Modest dress, conservative.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: PEK (Beijing Capital), PKX (Beijing Daxing), PVG (Shanghai Pudong), CAN (Guangzhou) major hubs. Air China, China Eastern, China Southern flag carriers. No regional consolidator standard. Direct booking typical.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Visa required for most nationalities. 144-hour visa-free transit for 53 countries (must depart to different country). 72-hour visa-free in some cities. Passport valid 6 months beyond stay. Chinese embassy/consulate visa application.

Climate & Weather: Varied by region. Beijing: -10°C (Jan) to 30°C (July). Shanghai: 4°C to 32°C. Guangzhou: 14°C to 33°C. Hong Kong: 15°C to 31°C. Check specific destination. Air pollution can be severe in winter.

Apparel Sourcing: Conservative dress. Modest clothing recommended. Religious sites: cover shoulders/knees. Size system: Chinese sizing smaller than Western. Winter: heavy coats in north, lighter in south.

arrival24h.simple: Power: 220V, 50Hz, Type A/C/I sockets. 4G/5G excellent, no foreign eSIM. Alipay/WeChat Pay mandatory for payments. Airport Express trains.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 220V, 50Hz. Type A (US-style), Type C (Europlug), Type I (angled pins) sockets. Type I most common. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-i/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 100+ Mbps. 4G coverage 99%, 5G extensive. ISPs: China Mobile, China Unicom, China Telecom. **No foreign eSIM** - must get local SIM (China Unicom best for tourists). Great Firewall blocks Google, Facebook, Twitter.

Financial Rails: **Cashless society** - Alipay and WeChat Pay mandatory for most transactions. Foreign credit cards rarely accepted. Cash only in some places. No tipping culture. VPN needed for blocked services.

Airport-to-City: Beijing PEK: Airport Express train (¥25, 20min) or taxi (~¥100-150). Shanghai PVG: Maglev (¥50, 8min) + Metro, or taxi (~¥200). Official apps: Alipay for payments.

mobility.simple: Extensive metro systems (Beijing 24 lines, Shanghai 16 lines). Didi ride-hailing (no Uber). Bike share everywhere. Walking variable, crowded streets.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Beijing: 24 Metro lines, 400+ stations. Shanghai: 16 Metro lines, extensive network. Guangzhou: 14 lines. Integrated transit cards (Yikatong). Apps: Metro China, Citymapper. English signage in major cities.

Informal Transit: Limited. Some unofficial minibus routes, but formal systems dominant.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Didi Chuxing (Chinese Uber) - requires Alipay/WeChat. No Uber/Bolt. Bike-sharing: Meituan, Hellobike (scan QR with phone). E-scooters: limited.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Variable. Excellent in modern districts, crowded in older areas. Jaywalking common despite being illegal. Sidewalks often blocked by parked scooters. Pedestrian crossings: cars may not yield.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Meituan, Ele.me dominant. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: OTC limited, many Rx-only. Tap water not safe - boil or use bottles.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Meituan, Ele.me (food). JD.com, Taobao (shopping). Grocery delivery: Hema Fresh, Meituan Select. 24/7 delivery culture.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, convenience stores. No state monopoly. Drinking age 18. Baijiu (white spirit) culture. No tipping.

Pharmacy: Limited OTC. Many medications Rx-only. Pharmacies: Yifang, major chains. Language barrier can be issue.

Beverage & Dietary: **Tap water not safe** - must boil or use bottled water. Zero-sugar options available. Local: baijiu, green tea, soymilk. Rice/noodle-based cuisine. Chopsticks required.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Sharing dishes communal. No restrictions on plate refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid clocks (death), umbrellas (separation). Fruit/alcohol OK. Shoes removed in homes. Dogs generally not indoors. Respect hierarchy, face-saving, no tipping.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Avoid: clocks (sounds like 'death'), umbrellas (sounds like 'separation'), sharp objects. Acceptable: fruit, alcohol, tea, regional specialties. Refuse initially, accept after insistence. Wrap in red/gold (avoid white/black).

Household Norms: Shoes removed in homes. Slippers provided. Bathroom shoes often separate.

Companion Pet Culture: Dogs kept indoors in cities. Less dog-friendly in restaurants (rare). Stray dogs in rural areas. Pet ownership increasing.

Behavioral Matrix: Collectivist, hierarchy-focused. Respect for elders and authority. Face-saving crucial. Indirect communication. Punctuality: on-time expected. No tipping (can be offensive). Physical greetings: handshake or slight bow. Business cards: two-handed exchange. Table manners: share dishes, don't stick chopsticks upright (resembles death).

preArrival.simple: Direct booking on JAL/ANA. Visa-free for 68 countries (90 days). Varied climate: Tokyo 5°C to 30°C, Okinawa 18°C to 32°C. Modest dress, conservative.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: NRT (Tokyo Narita), HND (Tokyo Haneda), KIX (Osaka Kansai) major hubs. JAL, ANA flag carriers. Skymark, Peach budget carriers. Direct booking typical. No regional consolidator standard.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Visa-free for 68 countries (US, Canada, EU, UK, Australia) - 90 days. Electronic Travel Authorization (eVISA) for some. Visa required for others. Passport valid 6 months beyond stay.

Climate & Weather: Varied by region. Tokyo: 5°C (Jan) to 30°C (July). Osaka: 4°C to 33°C. Hokkaido: -7°C to 26°C. Okinawa: 18°C to 32°C. Rainy season Jun-Jul, typhoon season Sep-Oct. Pack layers.

Apparel Sourcing: Conservative dress norms. Modest clothing recommended. Religious sites: cover shoulders/knees, remove shoes at temples. Size system: Japanese sizing (smaller than Western). Uniqlo, Muji local brands.

arrival24h.simple: Power: 100V, 50/60Hz, Type A/B sockets (flat pins). 4G/5G excellent, eSIM available. Cash still common (yen). Narita Express train to Tokyo.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 100V, 50Hz (east Japan) or 60Hz (west Japan). Type A (two flat pins) and Type B (two flat + ground pin) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-a/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 200+ Mbps. 4G coverage 99%, 5G extensive. ISPs: NTT Docomo, au, SoftBank. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Ubigi. Local SIM: Sakura Mobile (~$40/week).

Financial Rails: Cash still widely used (yen coins). NFC contactless growing (Suica, PASMO cards, Apple Pay). Credit cards accepted in cities. No mobile money. No tipping culture.

Airport-to-City: Tokyo NRT: Narita Express (¥3,070, 1 hour) or Keisei Skyliner (¥2,470, 40min). Osaka KIX: Haruka Express (¥1,830, 75min). Taxi very expensive (~¥20,000-30,000).

mobility.simple: Extensive rail networks (JR, private lines). No informal transit. No Uber (taxi apps only). Bike share systems. Excellent walkability, remove shoes indoors.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Tokyo: JR Yamanote Line, Metro (13 lines), private railways. Osaka: JR, Metro (8 lines). Integrated IC cards (Suica, PASMO, ICOCA). Apps: Japan Transit Planner, Google Maps (excellent).

Informal Transit: Limited. Formal systems dominate. No Matatus/Marshrutka-style informal transit.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: No Uber (regulations). Taxi apps: GO, MK Taxi. Bike-sharing: Docomo Bike Share, Hello Cycling. E-scooters: limited.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Excellent walkability. Sidewalks well-maintained. Pedestrian crossings respected by cars. Remove shoes in homes, ryokan, some restaurants. escalator etiquette: stand left, walk right (Tokyo).

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Uber Eats, Demae-can, Wolt. Alcohol: convenience store sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water safe. Convenience stores ubiquitous.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Uber Eats, Demae-can, Wolt. Local: Rakuten Delivery. Grocery delivery: Ito Yokado, Aeon. Convenience stores (konbini) 24/7: 7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in convenience stores, supermarkets, vending machines. No state monopoly. Drinking age 20. Sake, shochu culture. No tipping.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only. Pharmacies: in drugstores (Matsukiyo, Cocokara). Convenience stores sell basic OTC.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water potable nationwide, excellent quality. Zero-sugar options available. Local: green tea, Pocari Sweat, Calpis. Rice, fish, vegetables staple. Convenience store culture (onigiri, bento).

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Viking (Western-style buffet) popular. Sharing dishes not typical. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid white lilies (funerals), food items OK. Shoes removed in homes. Less dog-friendly indoors. Bowing etiquette, punctuality, quiet public behavior.
socialCode.detailed:

Companion Pet Culture: Less dog-friendly indoors. Dogs in restaurants rare (patios only). Strict leash laws. Pet cafes popular. Stray dogs rare.

Behavioral Matrix: Collectivist, harmony-focused. Bowing etiquette (depth varies by status). Punctuality essential (5-10 min early is on-time). Indirect communication. No tipping (can be offensive). Quiet in public (no phone calls on trains). Cleanliness highly valued. Group orientation.

preArrival.simple: For Laos, compare flights via Bangkok or Hanoi with Google Flights/Skyscanner; AirAsia MOVE and Traveloka can help stitch regional legs. Check Laos e-Visa eligibility by nationality.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Vientiane (VTE) is the main gateway; Luang Prabang (LPQ) and Pakse (PKZ) serve regional itineraries. Compare broad search with AirAsia MOVE/Traveloka for Southeast Asian connections, then verify routes with Lao Airlines and the operating carrier.

Entry: Laos e-Visa eligibility, ports of entry, and stay conditions are passport-specific. Check the official eVisa portal before booking and use only listed border checkpoints.

Climate and packing: Tropical monsoon climate, with hot/rainy and cooler/drier periods; northern highlands can be cooler. Check forecasts, bring rain protection and modest temple clothing.

arrival24h.simple: Laos uses 230 V / 50 Hz and Type A, B, C, E, and F sockets; check the specific lodging outlet. Keep kip cash for small payments and network outages.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz; Type A, B, C, E, and F outlets are reported. Check the plug at your lodging and device label; an adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and money: Check roaming/SIM availability and registration. The Lao kip (LAK) is local currency; cash is useful, especially outside Vientiane. Card and wallet acceptance is venue-dependent.

Airport transfer: VTE and LPQ have local transfer options that change. Confirm the airport's current passenger information, use marked taxi counters or hotel-arranged transport, and agree the fare before departure.

mobility.simple: Vientiane mainly uses buses and taxis; Loca ride-hailing coverage is city-specific. Laos-China Railway is useful for major north-south stops; book through official channels.
mobility.detailed:
Vientiane: City buses serve selected corridors; check current timetables and payment locally. Loca is a local ride app, but coverage depends on location and network access.

Intercity: Laos-China Railway connects Vientiane with northern destinations; confirm current timetable, station, ticket name, and boarding rules through the official railway/booking channel. Coaches serve other routes.

Walking: Heat, limited sidewalks, and traffic can make walking difficult outside central districts. Plan short routes, use marked crossings, and avoid assuming rural transport runs frequently.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery-app coverage is limited and address-dependent outside Vientiane. Use sealed or treated water and carry essential medicines for rural travel.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Daily services: Delivery and grocery apps have limited coverage; ask your accommodation which service currently reaches the address. Cash may be needed for small shops and transport.

Health and water: Do not assume tap water is potable. Use sealed bottled or properly treated water. Pharmacies are less comprehensive outside larger towns; carry essential medication in original packaging and check import rules.

Food and dining: Lao food often uses herbs, sticky rice, and shared dishes; ask about fish sauce, allergens, and spice. Service and buffet rules vary by venue; check before ordering.

socialCode.simple: At temples, cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes where instructed. Ask before photographing people or ceremonies; follow a host's cues at home.
socialCode.detailed:
Temples and homes: Dress modestly at religious sites and remove shoes where asked. In homes, ask your host about footwear and gifts.

Monastic settings: Do not touch monks without invitation; follow posted visitor rules and ask before photographing ceremonies or people.

Dining and language: Lao is the primary language; English availability varies. Be courteous, ask about ingredients, and follow the host's lead on shared food.

preArrival.simple: AirAsia MOVE for SE Asia budget flights. Visa-free for 90 days (161 countries). Hot tropical climate: 26°C to 33°C. Modest dress, conservative for mosques.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: KUL (Kuala Lumpur), PEN (Penang) major hubs. Malaysia Airlines (flag carrier), AirAsia MOVE (budget). Direct booking typical. AirAsia MOVE for SE Asia stitching.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Visa-free 90 days for 161 countries (US, EU, UK, Japan, Australia). Visa on arrival for some. Visa required for others. Passport valid 6 months beyond stay. Malaysian eVISA available.

Climate & Weather: Tropical. Kuala Lumpur: 26°C (Jan) to 33°C (April). Penang: 26°C to 32°C. Hot humid year-round, monsoon Oct-Mar. Pack lightweight, breathable fabrics, rain gear.

Apparel Sourcing: Modest dress norms. Cover shoulders/knees in mosques (women may need headscarf). Beach culture on islands. Size system: Asian sizing (smaller). Local brands: Padini, MANGO.

arrival24h.simple: Power: 240V, 50Hz, Type G sockets (UK-style). 4G/5G good, eSIM available. Touch 'n Go payment widespread. Grab ride-hailing. KLIA Ekspres to city.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 240V, 50Hz. Type G (British 3-pin) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-g/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 100+ Mbps. 4G coverage 95%, 5G in cities. ISPs: Maxis, Celcom, Digi. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: Maxis (~RM50/week).

Financial Rails: Touch 'n Go (card/app) ubiquitous for transit. Cash still used. GrabPay, TNG eWallet for mobile payments. Tipping: not expected (10% for excellent service).

Airport-to-City: Kuala Lumpur KUL: KLIA Ekspres (RM55, 35min) or KLIA Transit (RM25, 45min). Grab ride-hailing (~RM60-80 to center). Official taxi: coupon system.

mobility.simple: KL MRT/LRT/Monorail (extensive). No informal transit. Grab ride-hailing dominant. Bike share limited. Variable walkability, covered walkways.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Kuala Lumpur: MRT (2 lines), LRT (3 lines), Monorail, buses. Integrated Touch 'n Go card. Penang: Rapid Penang buses. Apps: MyRapid, Moovit. Covered walkways in KL.

Informal Transit: Limited. Formal systems dominate. No Matatus/Marshrutka-style informal transit.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Grab dominant. No Uber. No Bolt. Bike-sharing: limited. E-scooters: limited.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Variable. Good in Bukit Bintang, KLCC. Covered walkways in KL (climate control). Sidewalk quality varies. Pedestrian crossings: use zebra crossings, traffic may not yield. Climate: hot/humid, outdoor walking tiring.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: GrabFood, Foodpanda, ShopeeFood. Alcohol: supermarket sales, Muslim-majority (limited). Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water not safe.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: GrabFood, Foodpanda, ShopeeFood. Local: Dahmakan. Grocery delivery: Tesco, Jaya Grocer. 24/7 convenience stores: 7-Eleven, 99 Speedmart.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, non-Muslim areas. Muslim-majority country - alcohol restricted (sold in non-Muslim areas, licensed premises). Drinking age 18. No tipping.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only. Pharmacies: Watsons, Guardian, independent. Convenience stores sell basic OTC.

Beverage & Dietary: **Tap water not safe** - use bottled water. Zero-sugar options available. Local: teh tarik, kopi O, coconut water. Nasi lemak, roti canai, laksa staple. Halal food predominant.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Buffet restaurants popular. Halal buffets available. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid pork/alcohol for Muslim hosts, fruit/food OK. Shoes removed in homes. Dog-friendly limited (Muslim sensitivity). Respect Islam, 'face-saving', relaxed pace.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: acceptable. Avoid alcohol/pork for Muslim hosts. Fruit, high-quality items appropriate. Presentation important. Receive with right hand.

Household Norms: Shoes removed in homes. Follow host's lead.

Companion Pet Culture: Less dog-friendly (Muslim sensitivity). Dogs in restaurants rare. Cats more common as pets. Stray dogs fed by locals.

Behavioral Matrix: Collectivist, harmony-focused. Muslim-majority (Islam). Respect for Ramadan (no eating/drinking in public during fasting). Punctuality: 30-60 min grace socially (Malaysia Boleh - relaxed attitude). Tipping: not expected. Right hand for eating/giving. Head/feet taboo (don't touch). 'Face-saving' important. Multicultural (Malay, Chinese, Indian).

preArrival.simple: For Southeast Asia, compare AirAsia MOVE and Traveloka with Google Flights/Skyscanner; Scoot is an airline, not a search engine. Check Thailand e-Visa eligibility by passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight search and routing: Bangkok (BKK/DMK) is the main hub; Chiang Mai, Phuket, and other cities serve regional trips. AirAsia MOVE and Traveloka are regional booking platforms; Scoot is a carrier. Compare with Google Flights/Skyscanner, then check baggage and airport with the airline.

Entry: Thailand's e-Visa application is online, but eligibility and required documents depend on nationality and current policy. Use the official Thai e-Visa portal and the relevant embassy; do not assume visa-on-arrival or visa-free access.

Climate and packing: Hot/humid conditions year-round, with regional monsoon and cooler northern-season variation. Check forecasts, heat and air-quality alerts; pack rain protection and modest temple clothing.

arrival24h.simple: Thailand uses 220 V / 50 Hz with Type A, B, C, F, and O sockets; bring a compatible adapter. PromptPay is domestic infrastructure, not guaranteed for visitors.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz; Type A, B, C, F, and O socket patterns are reported. Check your accommodation and device labels; an adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and payments: Buy a SIM/eSIM through a recognized provider and check registration requirements. PromptPay QR is common domestically, but visitors may not be able to link it; keep THB cash and an international card.

Airport transfers: Bangkok BKK and DMK have separate rail, bus, and taxi options. Check Airports of Thailand and the airport's current transport page; use marked taxi queues or official app pickup zones.

mobility.simple: Bangkok combines BTS, MRT, buses, and boats; Rabbit and stored-value products are not universally interchangeable. Grab, Bolt, and local motorcycle taxis cover many urban areas.
mobility.detailed:
Bangkok: BTS, MRT, Airport Rail Link, river boats, and buses use distinct operators and ticket rules. Check current routes and which cards/payment methods are accepted before transferring.

Ride-hailing: Grab and Bolt are available in many cities; use the app pickup point and check vehicle/plate. Motorcycle taxis are useful for short trips but helmets and road conditions matter.

Intercity: Trains, coaches, and domestic flights connect regions. Book through the official operator or recognized provider and verify station/airport, especially for overnight services.

dailyLiving.simple: LINE MAN and GrabFood serve many urban areas; check exact-address coverage. Water, pharmacy, alcohol-sale hours, and payment access vary by location and rules.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shopping: LINE MAN and GrabFood are common city examples; confirm address, phone, cash/card options, and operating hours in-app. 7-Eleven is widespread but not every branch stocks the same products.

Water and pharmacy: Use sealed or reliably filtered water unless your accommodation confirms local guidance. Pharmacies are common in cities; check prescription rules for medicines you bring.

Food and payment: Ask about spice, fish sauce, allergens, and dietary needs. Alcohol sales are subject to Thai law and local restrictions; check current rules and posted hours rather than relying on old summaries.

socialCode.simple: At temples, cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes where directed. Avoid touching people's heads or pointing feet at sacred images; ask before photos.
socialCode.detailed:
Temples: Follow posted dress rules, remove shoes where instructed, and observe signs restricting photography or access. Keep feet pointed away from Buddha images and altars.

Greetings and public conduct: A wai may be appropriate, but context varies; a polite verbal greeting is also fine. Keep interactions respectful and avoid confrontations in public.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Customs differ by household; follow the host's lead.

arrival24h.simple: Vietnam uses 110/220 V at 50 Hz with Type A, C, and D sockets; check the accommodation's outlet type. Carry some VND and confirm SIM/eSIM registration options.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 110/220 V at 50 Hz; Type A, C, and D sockets are reported. Supply varies by location/building. Check device input and use an adapter; it does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and payments: Check local SIM/eSIM requirements and roaming before landing. QR wallets such as MoMo and ZaloPay are primarily domestic; do not assume visitors can activate them. Keep Vietnamese dong (VND) and a card backup.

Airport transfer: Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City airports have official bus, taxi, and app pickup options. Confirm the airport, pickup zone, and current route; use an official counter or verified in-app vehicle.

mobility.simple: Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have metro lines alongside buses; Grab, Be, and Xanh SM operate in many cities. Intercity trains use Vietnam Railways booking.
mobility.detailed:
City transit: Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have metro services alongside buses; routes, hours, and fare systems are still expanding. Use the local operator or station signage for current information.

Ride-hailing and informal travel: Grab, Be, and Xanh SM are options in major urban areas; confirm vehicle details and fare in-app. Xe ôm motorcycle taxis may be app-booked or negotiated; agree terms before riding.

Intercity and walking: Vietnam Railways sells official train tickets; check station names and travel time. Sidewalks can be occupied by parked motorbikes; cross slowly and predictably at marked points.

dailyLiving.simple: GrabFood and ShopeeFood cover many city addresses; confirm coverage in-app. Use bottled water unless local accommodation gives reliable advice for that building.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: GrabFood and ShopeeFood are common urban options. Coverage, phone-number requirements, cash/card support, and operating hours depend on exact address.

Water and pharmacy: Do not assume tap water is potable. Use sealed bottled water or suitable treatment. Pharmacies are common in cities, but bring essential medicine in original packaging and verify import rules.

Food and payment: Cash in VND remains useful alongside cards and domestic wallets. Ask about ingredients, spice, and allergens. Buffet terms and refill rules are venue-specific.

socialCode.simple: At temples, dress modestly and remove shoes where instructed. Ask before photographing people; use two hands when offering or receiving items if that is the host's cue.
socialCode.detailed:
Temples and homes: Follow posted footwear and clothing rules. Ask whether to remove shoes in a home and follow the host's lead.

Dining and gifts: Ask about dietary needs and observe how shared dishes are served. A small food gift may be welcome, but ask about preferences and avoid assumptions about taboos.

Photography and greetings: Ask permission before photographing people or ceremonies. Greetings vary by age and setting; a polite verbal greeting is a safe default.
